THE_STANDING_RULE: A LANDING IS PROVEN BY A COUNT AT A FETCHED REF, NEVER BY A COMMIT SHA IN PROSE.
THE_PATH_TO_STEP_MAPPING_IS_DAS_ATTRIBUT: it is this ledger's weakest link: a status keyed on a path nobody declared measures the guess, not the lane. `unattributed_lane_files` is the guard.
WHY_V2: DA 274: every row is now COMPUTED at verification time from a FETCHED ref. v1 carried statuses copied from reports and was ALREADY STALE when it landed -- it recorded step 2 as NOT LANDED ON ANY REF after measuring be_sigma_30m.py at 0 of 3; it is 1 of 2 executing refs now. The row was true when written and false when read, which is what a copied status always eventually is.

TWO_DEFECTS_IN_THIS_INSTRUMENT_THAT_I_FO.1_cwd_dependence: the first _count() ran  without -C, so from live/pm_research every path resolved to live/pm_research/live/pm_research/... and EVERY COUNT CAME BACK 0. The ledger reported the whole lane unlanded including a file I had verified minutes earlier. IT PASSED THE FALSIFIER because every cell was a NEGATIVE control -- an absent path counts 0 -- and a function returning 0 for everything satisfies all of them. Fixed with git -C <toplevel> and a POSITIVE control that a known-landed path counts 1.
TWO_DEFECTS_IN_THIS_INSTRUMENT_THAT_I_FO.2_guessed_paths: step 4 was keyed on de_canonical_forecast_action / de_forecast_action_scorer, names I invented. The real files are de_canonical_action_population and de_fair_value_actions, so step 4 read NO_FILES while two of its files sat on both refs. A status keyed on a path nobody declared measures the GUESS, not the lane. Fixed, and guarded by unattributed_lane_files.
TWO_DEFECTS_IN_THIS_INSTRUMENT_THAT_I_FO.the_class: both are FALSE NEGATIVES PRODUCED BY THE INSTRUMENT rather than by the world, and both read as findings.

WHAT_SATISFIED_MEANS_HERE: presence on both executing refs AND a driven-green behaviour verdict from the owning seat. Presence alone gives LANDED_BEHAVIOUR_UNVERIFIED -- which is why gates_satisfied is 1 and not 6 despite six steps having files.
